note: Polarity control for recordguardctl. Every fixture is a drafts/self-review record extracted VERBATIM from git; `provenance` gives the blob id and the commit:path it came from, so the fixture cannot drift away from the history it claims to represent. `history/` holds records that still said they were unfinished; `real/` holds finished records a landing decision may rest on. `expect` declares the EXACT signal rows each fixture must produce as `line|signal|term`, sorted — not a count and not a boolean, so that deleting any ONE signal from the discriminator shows up here instead of being masked by another signal still firing on the same file. Three of the `real/` fixtures are adversarial controls: `div05-close-overtakes-echo-FINAL.md` is the SAME PATH as `history/div05-close-overtakes-echo-STUB.md` after the branch finished (the differential — same file, opposite verdict); `F009-quotes-the-stub.md` quotes that stub's text verbatim inside a `*"..."*` span and must stay silent, which is the only thing forcing quote-awareness; `F001-shortest-real-record.md` is 7 lines long, shorter than every stub in `history/`, which is what forbids a length threshold. This manifest is read by `go run ./cmd/recordguardctl gate` on every gates run, not only by `go test`.

cases.why: F009's motivating instance. The `claude/div05-close-overtakes-echo` branch carried this nine-line stub behind seven commits and 983 insertions of finished-looking code; the loop judged the branch reviewed by counting files matching `drafts/self-review` and reported all three wave-4 branches complete. Landing it would have put an unreviewed behaviour-bearing change on mainline. A detector that cannot catch this instance is not a detector, so this fixture is the one that must never go silent.

A second real stub with DIFFERENT wording: it says `No findings yet` rather than `Nothing verified yet`, and its status value is `stub pushed to protect against container restart` with no occurrence of `in progress` at all. It is here because a lexicon fitted to div05 alone would miss it. The same path is 459 real lines on mainline today, and its title was rewritten when the work became real.

A third wording again: `Status: started.` — no `in progress`, no `WIP` in the status value, and no void phrase anywhere. Only the title marker and the word `started` carry it. It is the fixture that forces `started` into the lexicon.

A stub with sixteen lines of real problem statement, two numbered findings-to-be and eight evidence tokens — more citation than several REAL records carry. It is the fixture that forbids reading evidence density as the primary signal: only the record's own `Status: STUB.` separates it from finished work.

A stub whose TITLE is clean — `raising the projection ceiling`, no marker — so the title signal cannot carry it, and whose findings section is the literal placeholder `(to be filled in — nothing claimed yet)`. It is the fixture that forces `to be filled in` and `nothing claimed yet` into the void lexicon.

Working notes carrying 42 lines of real evidence — plane tables, a merge-base, blob-sha borrow receipts — and NO status-declaration line at all. Two things carry it: the title qualifier `(WIP)`, and a `## Status` checklist with three unchecked boxes. It is the fixture that forces the title signal and the open-checklist signal to exist independently of the status line, and the honest-in-progress case in its purest form: this record is CORRECT as written, and the tool refuses it as a landing precondition rather than faulting it.

THE DIFFERENTIAL. Same repository path as the first fixture, 552 lines instead of 9, after the branch actually finished; its line 3 now reads `STATUS: COMPLETE for what it claims`. Same file, same signal position, opposite verdict — which is what shows the discriminator is reading the status VALUE and not merely noticing that a status line exists. If this fires, the tool is punishing a finished record.

QUOTE CONTROL. This finding quotes the div05 stub verbatim — `*"STATUS: IN PROGRESS — stub pushed early to survive container restarts. … Nothing verified yet."*` — inside a paired double-quote span on line 4. It is a finished record. It is the only fixture that forces the discriminator to distinguish the record's own voice from a quotation, and without that distinction the tool would refuse the very finding that motivated it.

LENGTH CONTROL. Seven lines — shorter than five of the six `history/` stubs and shorter than the nine-line div05 stub — and completely finished: what happened, what it cost, the deciding moment, the evidence, the bin. It is the fixture that forbids any length threshold, and the reason `cites-nothing` is pinned at literally zero rather than at a fitted floor.

The shortest LANDING record in the tree at 39 lines: exit codes read from the process, trees compared, nine files named. A landing decision rests on exactly this shape of record, so it must be accepted.

cases.provenance: git blob b9cdf813ef09f28d2569bcdfcf7a2e2febebe6a4 = drafts/self-review/adapter-residuals.md at HEAD
cases.why: 421 lines. Named in F009 as the branch that DID land in the same firing div05 was held back from, because it carried a real record. Silence here is the other half of the historical claim.

442 lines, and the record of the sibling detector this tool is modelled on. It discusses stubs, WIP, RED readings and deletion attacks at length, which makes it the densest available test of whether the discriminator is reading declarations or merely matching vocabulary.

cases.provenance: hand-written; the only fixture here that is not a real record. Added after deletion attack A7 (word-boundary check removed) SURVIVED the twelve real fixtures.
cases.why: WORD-BOUNDARY CONTROL. A finished record in which six words each contain a lexicon term as a substring — `drafts` holds `draft`, `restarted` holds `started`, `stubbed` holds `stub`, `wiped` holds `wip`, `appending` holds `pending`, `incompleteness` holds `incomplete` — placed in the title and in the status VALUE, where the title and status signals read. No real record in the corpus happens to do this, so nothing else in the manifest can catch a discriminator that matches the lexicon without word boundaries.
